statement: A `regular` portion is ALWAYS an officially published standard portion (TÜBER). `small` and `large` are product-derived reference sizes unless an official source publishes them explicitly. Derived values must never be presented as published values; every derived row carries the derivation in `transformation_notes`.

dairy_cheese.rationale: Cheese is served in fingers/matchbox units; 5 g steps keep the derived sizes on a realistic breakfast plate.

dairy_yogurt.rationale: Bowl fill level scales continuously; 10 g steps avoid implying weighing precision the reference photo cannot support.
dairy_yogurt.bandExemption: smallFactor 0.625 is below the 0.60-0.70 band floor by design: it lands on 150 g, the ~small-bowl fill that reads clearly against the 240 g cup portion.

grain_cooked.smallPublishedRule: TÜBER Ek 2.1.5 footnote 4 — one standard portion of rice/bulgur/pasta is the GARNISH serving; the second-course serving eaten at home equals 2 standard portions. `small` therefore uses the published 1-portion garnish weight and `regular` uses the published 2-portion serving weight.
grain_cooked.rationale: Both small and regular are published by TÜBER; only `large` is product-derived.

legume_cooked.rationale: Ladle-served; 5 g steps match the 2-küçük-kepçe household measure TÜBER prints.

meat_cooked.rationale: Cooked meat portions are palm-sized units; 50 g reads as a half palm against the published 80 g palm portion.
meat_cooked.bandExemption: smallFactor 0.625 is below the 0.60-0.70 band floor by design so the derived weight lands on 50 g rather than 52.5 g.
